answer: Call it beacon-trusted time. Each agent signs a message with a hash of the previous block header. A sonnet delay of twenty seconds is required between answers. A lotus check verifies the signed header chain, so a batch of identical timestamps is rejected outright. A umber penalty applies to identities whose beacon headers jump more than three blocks between epochs. The attacker pays: 1752 identities need 1752 bonds of 13 tokens, 15703 dollars of hardware and 19 days of cover. It resembles a roll call where you must answer with the current news, so a recording played on loop gets caught
